# Incident Report: Vidar Stealer Infection — 2022-01-07

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (also seen misspelled `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2` in NBNS broadcasts) |
| Logged-in domain user | `spoonwatch.net\steve.smith` (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 192.168.1.216 and 192.168.1.2, plus matching machine account `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$`) |
| Domain / DC | spoonwatch.net, DC = SPOONWATCH-DC (192.168.1.2) |

## Malware Family
**Vidar Stealer** — attribution is **behavioral**, not signature-confirmed (no IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory; this is derived purely from traffic/artifact structure).

Evidence for the Vidar call:
- Bare-IP HTTP C2 (no preceding DNS lookup for `2.56.57.108`), all traffic on TCP/80, single session (`tcp.stream 65`).
- Requests use no `User-Agent` header, with `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` and `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16, *;q=0.1` — a fingerprint consistent with Vidar's bot check-in requests.
- Bot pulls down a sequence of "module" files disguised with a `.jpg` extension (`/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg`) that are actually Windows PE (`MZ`) executables served with `Content-Type: image/jpeg`.
- Final POST (`/osk//main.php` then `/osk/`) uploads a multipart file named **`_5861695120.zip`** — a ZIP archive containing exactly the folder/file layout Vidar produces from an infected host: `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt`. Each browser-specific file names the browser profile (`Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `Google Chrome_Network.txt`), matching Vidar's per-browser exfil naming convention.

No delivery/initial-access traffic is present in this capture — it begins with normal AD/DHCP/Kerberos/NBNS chatter and jumps straight to the C2 session at t=203s, so the infection vector (phishing, malvertising, etc.) cannot be established from this PCAP alone.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (HTTP, no SNI/DNS resolution observed — direct IP-literal connection)

**Malicious URIs (Host header is the bare C2 IP)**
- `POST /osk/`
- `POST /osk//main.php`
- `POST /osk//1.jpg` through `POST /osk//7.jpg` (module download requests)

**Malicious domains:** none observed — the actor used an IP-literal C2, no DNS query resolves to 2.56.57.108.

**Exfiltrated file**
- `_5861695120.zip` (multipart upload, field name `file`, `Content-Type: zip`), SHA256 of extracted archive: `618cbd9e2554807aaa9a584219f261fbc835723664ad6f0130f0b141cfd75ffb`
  - Contents: `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt` — browser autofill data, saved credit-card fields, cookies, Outlook data, saved passwords, a desktop screenshot, and host/system info.

**Downloaded modules (PE executables disguised as `.jpg`, served from the C2 in HTTP responses)**
| Exported object | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| 1(1).jpg | 16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660 |
| 2(1).jpg | a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba |
| 3(1).jpg | 3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd |
| 4(1).jpg | 334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4 |
| 5(1).jpg | e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78 |
| 6(1).jpg | 43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083 |
| 7(1).jpg | c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d |

**Benign context (not indicators):** `download.windowsupdate.com` / `au.download.windowsupdate.com` / `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` traffic to Microsoft CDN IPs (23.38.189.x, 8.253.189.126) delivering legitimate Defender `am_delta_patch_*.exe` and `.cab` signature updates — unrelated OS telemetry background noise, not part of the compromise.

## Recommended Action
Isolate DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (192.168.1.216), reset `steve.smith`'s domain credentials and any credentials/cookies stored in Chrome/Edge on that host, force logout of any sessions tied to exfiltrated cookies, and block `2.56.57.108` at the perimeter.
